title: The Great Pacific Garbage Patch
passage: Between Hawaii and California lies a massive collection of debris known as the Great Pacific Garbage Patch. Despite its name, it is not a solid island of trash that you can walk on. Instead, it is a high concentration of plastics, chemical sludge, and other debris trapped by the currents of the North Pacific Gyre. A gyre is a large system of circulating ocean currents. Most of the patch is made of 'microplastics'—tiny pieces of plastic that are smaller than a pencil eraser. These particles are often invisible to the naked eye but are very dangerous. Marine animals like sea turtles and fish often mistake these bits of plastic for food. When they eat the plastic, it can make them very sick. Scientists are working on ways to clean up the ocean, but many believe the best solution is to stop plastic from entering the water in the first place by reducing waste and recycling.
